decisions.reason: After a second year on the market, the combined shuttering and de-shuttering robot appears to be the firm's core integrated automation option, so management would keep it because its strategic fit is high and the cost of keeping this option open is likely modest relative to its potential system value.

The stand-alone de-shuttering robot still merits staying on the market because it can address customers seeking partial automation, but its overlap with the combined system makes it the most exposed remaining machinery option if demand proves too narrow.

As a very recent multi-model launch tied to the firm's established process equipment range, this machine line would likely be kept while management learns which variants gain traction and because uncertainty about its full value is still unresolved.

Production analysis software is highly complementary to the firm's automation, service, and lifecycle support business, and its relatively low carrying cost gives management a strong real-options reason to keep developing and marketing it.
